summary: Asymmetric egress path causing TCP retransmit spike and inference timeouts for enterprise customer
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-11 02:15 UTC, NovaDocs reported intermittent request timeouts and elevated tail latency when calling the Redwood inference API. Preliminary captures show a sudden rise in TCP retransmits and out-of-order packets for flows between our edge egress proxies and the regional serving fleet. Impact: Customer experiencing 10-20% 5xx errors and frequent streaming disconnects during business hours; production traffic for several routes timed out after multiple retransmit attempts. Hypothesis: asymmetric egress path causing packet reordering and spurious retransmits leading to request stalls and streaming cancellation.
impact: ~12% of NovaDocs requests observed with >5s tail latency or cancelled streams between 2026-03-11 02:00-04:30 UTC. Affects enterprise contract SLAs; customer reported degraded UX for real-time summarization feature.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use NovaDocs prod API key and send 1k streaming generate requests to /v1/generate over us-east endpoint
2) Observe a 10-20% increase in aborted streams and >5s p95 on the customer route
3) Run tcpdump on egress-proxy-a and egress-proxy-b and compare sequence/ack patterns for affected flows
4) Reproduce shows bursty retransmits and duplicate ACKs when traffic traverses peering IX with AS path change
logs: 2026-03-11T02:18:22Z SERVING-01: TLS read timed out after 3200ms for request id=cd9f5
2026-03-11T02:20:10Z K8S-POD: high kubeproxy conntrack drops observed: conntrack: table full warnings
Capture note: load-balanced flows split across two egress peers with different AS path lengths; reordering observed when path switches mid-flow
investigation_notes: Observed correlation between BGP flaps on transit provider B and spike in retransmits for affected flows.
Net team verified no interface errors on egress proxies; packet captures show consistent out-of-order delivery and duplicate ACKs from downstream.
Serving runtime logs show requests stuck in read loop waiting for TLS payload; retries from client cause multiple inflight KV cache misses increasing tail latency.
Applied iptables rule to force symmetric egress via preferred peer on a cohort of flows and saw immediate drop in retransmits and p95 latency improvement for test traffic.
Possible contributing factor: conntrack table reaching high-watermark under sustained burst causing NAT state convergence delays.
Related telemetry: increased retransmit rate aligns with customer request bursts and small window of BGP route change at 02:17 UTC.
Linked to runbook: Network Path Troubleshooting; follow up with transit vendor for asymmetry mitigation and adjust conntrack sizing on egress proxies.
temporary_workaround: Pinned NovaDocs routes to egress-peer-1 via iptables MARK + policy routing for the customer prefix; this reduced retransmit rate and dropped error rate for pinned traffic to <1% during the test window.
next_steps: 1) SRE to request upstream transit vendor ticket for AS path stability and to review peer filtering (owner: NetOps, due 2026-03-13)
2) Increase conntrack table size on egress proxies and roll to canary (owner: Infra, due 2026-03-13)
3) Implement short-term request-level retry backoff in the api-gateway to avoid immediate client retransmit amplification (owner: API team, due 2026-03-14)
4) Re-run load test with NovaDocs key after changes and monitor retransmit / p95 metrics for 24h (owner: Support/SRE, due 2026-03-14)
5) Postmortem and customer RCA to be prepared after root cause confirmation (owner: Support, due 2026-03-17)

resolution: Mitigation applied: customer traffic pinned to stable egress peer and conntrack sizing increased in prod canary. Transit vendor is addressing BGP asymmetry. API gateway retry backoff deployed as a safety net. Follow-up: complete vendor fix and finalize postmortem. Customer notified and monitoring shows errors back to <1%.
